extracted.intended_audience: federal agency regulatory analysts and rule writers preparing regulatory analyses for proposed and final rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing regulatory analyses (benefit-cost and cost-effectiveness) to support federal rulemakings under Executive Order 12866 and related authorities, including required accounting statements and specialized legal analyses. Covers analytic methods, presentation, transparency, and statutory cross-checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of need for the proposed action
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the need for the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the problem the agency intends to address (including market failures or other compelling public needs), assess the significance of that problem, describe statutory or judicial directives and the extent of agency discretion, and show that government intervention is likely to do more good than harm. For market-failure rationales, describe failures qualitatively and quantitatively where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of alternative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: An examination of alternative approaches to achieve the regulatory objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and evaluate a manageable set of alternatives (balancing thoroughness and analytical capacity). Consider alternatives defined by statute, different compliance dates, enforcement methods, degrees of stringency, differential requirements by firm size or geography, performance versus design standards, market-oriented approaches (fees, permits, offsets), and informational measures. Explain the rationale for the alternatives selected for detailed analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of benefits and costs (quantitative and qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: An evaluation of the benefits and costs—quantitative and qualitative—of the proposed action and the main alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible quantify and monetize benefits and costs; when not possible, measure in physical units or describe qualitatively. Include non-quantified outcomes and indicate which are most important. Present summaries of benefit and cost estimates for each alternative including qualitative and non-monetized factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain causal links between rule actions and expected benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the actions required by the rule are linked to the expected benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each alternative, indicate mechanisms (e.g., how additional safety equipment will reduce risks) and identify expected undesirable side-effects and ancillary benefits to be added to direct benefits and costs as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify a clearly stated baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a baseline against which benefits and costs are defined (normally a 'no action' baseline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the 'no action' baseline and, where useful, a 'next best' alternative; ensure all benefit and cost comparisons are defined relative to the chosen baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify where possible and convert to monetary units
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify benefits and costs and convert to dollar amounts where feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop quantitative estimates and monetize them when possible (many quantified estimates are convertible with effort). If not monetizable, present physical-unit measures or qualitative descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-quantified effects and threshold (break-even) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: When important benefits or costs cannot be monetized, conduct threshold or break-even analysis and identify important non-quantified effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry out a threshold analysis to answer 'How small could the value of the non-quantified benefits be (or how large would non-quantified costs need to be) before the rule yields zero net benefits?' Indicate which non-quantified effects are most important and why, and exercise professional judgment about their likely impact on rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with affected parties and experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek out opinions of those affected and individuals/organizations with special knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult early and not just at final stages; use consultation to ensure relevant issues and data are captured. Consider expert input for uncertain parameters (e.g., Delphi methods) and peer review where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and disclosure of assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A good analysis is transparent: state assumptions, time horizon, discount rates, and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a qualified third party can see how estimates and conclusions were derived. Provide sensitivity analysis to show how results change with plausible assumption variations and document all data sources, models, and methodologies in appendices. Include an executive summary and standardized accounting statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of sources, models, and appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific references to all data sources and appendices documenting models and uncertainty analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite data and analyses, include appendices with model documentation where necessary, and ensure results of sensitivity and uncertainty analyses are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of benefit-cost analysis (BCA) where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Use benefit-cost analysis (BCA) to express both benefits and costs in monetary units when feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure incremental benefits and costs of more stringent alternatives to identify the alternative that maximizes net benefits. Do not rely on benefit-cost ratios alone (ratios can be misleading); emphasize net benefits (absolute difference). When some benefits cannot be monetized, exercise judgment and consider threshold analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cost-effectiveness analysis (CEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cost-effectiveness analysis (CEA) for major rulemakings where primary benefits are health/safety and a valid effectiveness measure exists, and as a complement to BCA when monetization is incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare CEA for major health/safety rulemakings with measurable effectiveness; perform BCA as well when valid monetary values can be assigned. Use incremental CEA rather than averages, construct consistent cost and effectiveness measures, and avoid double-counting. Prefer final outcomes (lives saved, life-years) over intermediate outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer final outcomes for effectiveness measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In CEA prefer final outcome measures (e.g., lives saved, life-years saved) rather than intermediate outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If outcome unit quality varies (e.g., acres of wetlands), ensure measures capture variability in value. Explain choice of effectiveness measure and use integrated metrics (QALYs, equivalent lives) when mortality and morbidity both matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEA: construct net-cost numerator correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: In CEA the numerator should reflect net costs (gross compliance cost minus cost savings and monetized ancillary benefits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all relevant societal costs, avoid double-counting, and subtract monetized ancillary benefits from gross costs to yield net cost. If some ancillary benefits cannot be monetized, acknowledge CEA overstatement of cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple measures of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Report results with multiple measures of effectiveness to provide different insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB does not require a specific effectiveness measure; explain which measures were selected and why, and consider reporting both integrated measures (QALYs) and simpler metrics (lives saved) especially when both mortality and morbidity are affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness in effectiveness measures and subgroup treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust and report effectiveness measures to ensure fair treatment of population subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adjusting life expectancy or quality-of-life measures, prefer population averages rather than subgroup-specific metrics dominated by one demographic or income group. Do not diminish life-years saved for disabled populations simply because of disability prevalence; base life-years on average cohort life expectancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider whether federal regulation is best (subsidiarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether federal regulation is the best way to solve the problem or whether other means (state/local action, antitrust, litigation) are preferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the geographic scope of the problem, advantages of state/local experimentation, potential duplication costs, harmonization with international rules, and whether state/local approaches might be more efficient. Examine whether reducing State/local regulation could be appropriate when federal action is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption against certain economic regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: A demanding burden of proof is required before adopting certain types of economic regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid price controls in competitive markets, production or sales quotas in competitive markets, mandatory uniform quality standards if voluntary or disclosure would suffice, and controls on entry except when indispensable for health/safety or managing common property resources. Provide strong justification where these are proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and evaluate market failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify major types of market failure (externalities, common property/public goods, market power, inadequate/asymmetric information) when justifying regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe failures qualitatively and, where feasible, quantitatively. For externalities explain transaction-cost/property-rights issues; for market power assess whether regulation increases or reduces market power; for information failures document whether market-provided information is inadequate and whether poor information processing warrants intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider alternative enforcement methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider different enforcement frameworks (on-site inspections, periodic reporting, penalties, random or parametric monitoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the enforcement method that provides appropriate incentives at least cost, compare monitoring alternatives for effectiveness and cost, and discuss tradeoffs in monitoring intensity and compliance assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider different compliance dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the timing of regulation and alternative compliance dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how delays or lead time affect benefits and costs (e.g., biological stocks, production planning) and consider phased or delayed compliance where it materially alters net benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider different degrees of stringency
rubrics_metrics.description: Study alternative levels of regulatory stringency and their effects on benefits and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze marginal costs and benefits across stringency levels to determine how size and distribution of benefits/costs change; present incremental comparisons among successive stringency levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different requirements for different sized firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider setting different regulatory requirements for large and small firms where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base differences on estimated compliance cost differences or expected benefits. Remember small entities may face larger relative costs and that rules affecting many small entities trigger the Regulatory Flexibility Act provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different requirements for different geographic regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider regional differentiation when benefits or costs vary significantly across regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze regional heterogeneity and consider geographically tailored requirements where appropriate; weigh benefits of localized policies against costs of regulatory fragmentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer performance standards over design standards when feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Use performance (outcome-based) standards rather than prescriptive design standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance standards typically give regulated parties flexibility to achieve objectives cost-effectively; account for monitoring/compliance costs when comparing flexibility benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore market-oriented approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider market-oriented instruments (fees, subsidies, tradable permits, offsets, changes in liability, bonds, insurance) as alternatives to direct controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether market mechanisms (e.g., averaging, banking, trading) can reduce costs or achieve benefits earlier, ensuring they do not create unacceptable local 'hot spots' or unintended distributional harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer informational measures for information failures
rubrics_metrics.description: When market failure arises from information problems, prefer informational remedies (testing/rating systems, disclosure, government provision of information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate costs of information collection/disclosure (including displaced information), potential misinterpretation, and incentives created. Consider least intrusive informational alternative sufficient to accomplish objectives and voluntary standards where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of benefits and costs over time (discounting and presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present undiscounted annual streams of benefits and costs and annualized estimates using specified discount rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present stream for each year of the analytic horizon beginning when the final rule begins to have effects. Provide annualized benefits/costs using real discount rates of 3% and 7%. Report monetized effects in 2001 dollars and convert using the GDP deflator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of risk and uncertainty (sensitivity and probabilistic analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide expected-value estimates and distributions; use sensitivity analysis and, for complex or very large rules, formal probabilistic analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report expected values and uncertainty bounds (95%/5% if only bounds). Use sensitivity analysis (one-variable or multivariable) to find 'switch points'. For complex rules or those exceeding $1 billion annually, apply formal probabilistic analyses (Monte Carlo, expert elicitation/Delphi) and pay attention to correlated inputs; display probabilistic results clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic valuation under uncertainty and risk preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: When outcomes have probability distributions, combine distributions and emphasize summary statistics; assume risk neutrality unless justified otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expected values (average/expected value) as summary measures, explain if adopting different risk-preference assumptions, and justify reasons for deviations from risk neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make alternative assumptions explicit and test them
rubrics_metrics.description: Make modeling and estimation assumptions explicit and perform sensitivity analyses using plausible alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rankings or net-benefit signs change under plausible alternative assumptions, conduct further analysis to adjudicate among assumptions and reveal hidden assumptions in estimation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision and rounding of reported estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported estimates should reflect analytical precision and appropriate rounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rounding conventions that reflect precision (e.g., $220 million rounded to nearest $10 million implies +/-$5 million). Avoid implying excessive precision; document precision conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate reporting of transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and report transfers separately; avoid misclassifying transfer payments as benefits or costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish transfers that are federal budget actions from transfers between private parties; use categories to describe major redistributive effects; report transfers separately (on-budget and off-budget) and note if transfers have associated efficiency effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting statement with standardized tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an accounting statement with tables reporting benefit and cost estimates for each major final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use suggested table format reporting primary/minimum/maximum estimates and source citations; report categories of benefits/costs (monetized, quantified but not monetized, qualitative) and impacts on governments, small businesses, wages, and growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of benefits and costs (mutually exclusive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify benefits and costs into three mutually exclusive categories: monetized, quantified but not monetized, and qualitative (not quantified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid double-counting across categories; use as many subcategories as needed to describe distinct effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report effects on state, local, and tribal governments, small businesses, wages and growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify portions of benefits, costs and transfers received by state/local/tribal governments and effects on small businesses, wages, and economic growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent feasible, quantify these effects; note that rules with annual costs under $1 billion likely have minimal effects on economic growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (RFA) for impacts on small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a regulatory flexibility analysis if the rule could have a significant impact on a substantial number of small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow agency guidelines, consider consulting SBA Chief Counsel for Advocacy, and comply with SBREFA consultation requirements for EPA and OSHA when applicable. Consider posting RFA on the internet for public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Act statement for large mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a written statement about benefits and costs if a rule may result in aggregate expenditures by governments or the private sector of $100 million or more in any one year (adjusted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical requirements under the Unfunded Mandates Act are similar to E.O. 12866 requirements and can often be satisfied by the same analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the rule creates information collection, paperwork, or recordkeeping burdens subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify the practical utility of information collections; obtain OMB approval for new collections imposed on 10 or more persons and secure valid OMB control numbers. Coordinate with agency CIO as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conform to Information Quality Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure data and analysis meet Information Quality Act standards and agency/OMB guidelines for information disseminated by agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess information quality using agency guidelines in conformance with OMB government-wide guidance; consult agency CIO and OMB's Statistical and Science Policy Branch as needed. This circular defines OMB's minimum quality standards for regulatory analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA compliance and environmental impact statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider environmental impacts under NEPA and prepare an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete NEPA documentation before issuing a final rule for major Federal actions significantly affecting the human environment; follow CEQ regulations and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impacts on children (Executive Order 13045)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address disproportionate risks to children from environmental health or safety risks when economically significant and applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide OMB/OIRA with an evaluation of the environmental health or safety effects on children and an explanation why the planned regulation is preferable to other feasible alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy impacts (Executive Order 13211)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a Statement of Energy Effects for significant energy actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed statement of adverse effects on energy supply, distribution, or use (shortfalls, price increases, increased foreign supply use) for the action and reasonable alternatives, and publish the Statement or summary in the NPRM and final rule when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal probabilistic analysis for very large/complex rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply formal probabilistic (e.g., Monte Carlo) analysis and expert elicitation for complex rules with cascading uncertainties or those exceeding $1 billion annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expert judgment (Delphi methods) to quantify parameter distributions, account for correlated inputs, run simulations to produce probability distributions of benefits and costs, and portray probabilistic results clearly in graphs/tables.
